A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we developed a pipeline to detect and correct the motion blur from aerial images provided by an airborne digital camera system with a channel dependent exposure times, which is a challenging task because of the high correlation between the three channels.
we propose a new method to estimate the motion blur from images shot by a channel dependent exposure time camera system.
the proposed pipeline is able to detect and correct the motion blur in aerial images with a high accuracy and robustness.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in the presence of motion blur, a phase based fusion of the three visible channels is more robust and efficient than a simple intensity based fusion.
the channel correlation is an effective tool for detecting motion blur and estimating blur parameters.
a channel dependent exposure time system is not only useful to increase the dynamic range of the image, but also to detect and correct motion induced blur.
